The original receiver-only calculation used a through-life diametral clearance of 60 µm. But the active guide is specified as 5.010–5.020 mm around a 4.995–5.000 mm stem. It can contribute another 25 µm.

Thus the construction has an optimistic 85 µm series deadband even before guide rocking.

I selected a total rotation limit of 0.35°, including unintended yaw. The corrected bound establishes neither that limit nor the 0.2 mm displacement limit.

An upper bound above a requirement is not a demonstrated physical failure. Nevertheless, it removes the claimed engineering certificate. At 85 µm, this conservative certificate would require approximately 306 MN/m, above the selected stem’s approximately 137 MN/m beam-plus-shear stiffness before other series compliance.

Assigning a larger complete-joint stiffness would therefore be an invalid repair. A different bearing, preload arrangement, shear path or geometry has to be physically constructed.

The executable shear sweep includes 6,137 cases and incompatible pattern-error vertices. Its smaller motions relative to a mathematical origin do not replace the arbitrary-initial-engagement clearance analysis.
